Fifteen comments

The Hare’s Paw

I got this one from Clare concertina player, Dymphna O’Sullivan. It’s a very simple but nice reel and was very popular with C

↳ Posted by Bannerman on February 24th, 2003.

Also known as “Kennedy’s Reel”

… You can find a recording of it under this name (available on CD now) in “The Sliabh Luachra Fiddle Master Padraig O‘Keeffe.” The CD notes about that tune that it “is named after a travelling fiddler who taught tunes to ’Bill the Waiver,’ Denis Murphy’s father.” Denis Murphy, of course, being the great Kerry fiddler around about Padraig’s time.

↳ Posted by pchaffee on May 8th, 2003.

Is in ‘The Northern Fiddler’ under the name ‘Low Park’

↳ Posted by prouse on July 16th, 2005.

They’ll Be Good Yet

Kitty Hayes and Peter Laban play this on their new cd, “They’ll Be Good Yet.” Kitty’s on a C concertina, so the Hare’s Paw comes out in F, which makes for a great fiddle setting as well.

Kerry version of Hare’s Paw

I got this from the new recording by the Boston-based band, Ivy Leaf. Here’s the provenance for the tune from their liner notes:

“The first tune is a local Kerry version of the Hare’s Paw. Padraig O’Keeffe was noted not only for commanding a repertoire of tunes from abroad, but also for producing lovely and unique settings which he passed on to his students; you can hear Padraig playing this one on The Sliabh Luachra Fiddle Master, and hear Denis Murphy playing it on Music from Sliabh Luachra – and if you’re lucky, Paddy Cronin having a go at it on an old private recording.”
